title: The soup that is never finished

data.source: 200 random contents and 200 coin flips, seeded.

prediction: The seed rule m' = q m + (1 - q) Phi is exactly simple exponential smoothing with alpha = 1 - q, the minimiser of a discounted least-squares sum, and the mean of a Bayes update that forgets at rate q; the differences are rounding error.
baseline: Brown's exponential smoothing (1956), discounted least squares, and conjugate Bayes with a forgetting factor.
why: Every identity held to rounding error; one side remark of mine about the circle was wrong and is recorded. The seed rule is exponential smoothing under another name, with a memory worth 1/(1 - q) occasions. The mathematics file says as much; nothing is left over.
